A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same geometric divergence and control framework. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across the substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original double-integrator and nonlinear cart-pole simulations, including feedback gains, trajectories, costs, and noise/regularization sensitivity results.

after.justification: V2 retains those simulations and additionally reports numerical feedback gains for a planar double integrator with anisotropic noise in Appendix C.7.

M1.justification: Section 5.1 adds finite-horizon regularization between whole-trajectory distributions and a closed-form control-sequence optimizer. V1 describes stagewise penalties and their finite-horizon Riccati extension; Appendix C.2 demonstrates that the new trajectory objective is different. V2 also corrects the extra factor of 1/2 on the divergence in the stated stagewise objective, while retaining the feedback formula.

E1.justification: V2 adds a planar double-integrator scenario with simultaneous low-noise and high-noise directions (Section 5.4; Appendix C.7). This extends the original isotropic-noise evaluations within the same control domain; the original double-integrator and cart-pole coverage remains.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons remain KL, WKL, and KWKL, including the added anisotropic example. FR and O are alternative labels for the retained KL and WKL constructions. Other divergences remain discussed rather than evaluated.

E3.justification: The added anisotropic evaluation specifies four states, two inputs, Q = I4, discount 0.9, lambda = 1, and noise covariance diag(10^-5, 10^-5, 10, 10). These are new experimental settings; the original simulation settings are retained. The trajectory-level extension is theoretical rather than an additional reported evaluation.

E4.justification: The new anisotropic case study tests how each regularizer treats different noise levels within one system and reports direction-specific feedback gains. The existing noise sweeps, lambda sensitivity analyses, nonlinear cart-pole trajectories, and divergence-ball illustrations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports simulation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added noise covariance describes the simulated environment, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Appendix C.7 adds numerical gain matrices and a directional comparison: WKL has the reported block [-0.3882, -1.1817] in both directions, while KWKL combines WKL-like and KL-like blocks. These are new results under a new setting, not improved scores for the earlier experiments. The original plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: V2 adds divergence properties and isometry proofs (Theorem 3.3), KWKL formulas for noncommuting Gaussian covariances under an invertibility assumption (Theorem A.3), and trajectory-control theory with a chain-rule counterexample (Appendix C.2-C.5). It corrects the Coulomb-divergence prefactor from 3/2 to 1/2, generalizes the affine covariance ODE, removes the previous lambda restriction and uses a pseudoinverse in Theorem 4.11, and narrows Theorem B.7 to Gaussians.

C1.justification: The abstract's broad statement that the divergences remain finite under support mismatch is narrowed to elliptic distributions with degenerating equal covariances. This substantially qualifies a headline guarantee. The central geometric construction and avoidance of low-noise control degeneracy remain the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 explicitly assumes an unproved geodesic-uniqueness conjecture. New Appendix D acknowledges missing existence/uniqueness criteria and the need for approximation outside structured families. Section 5.1 and Appendix C.2 explain why trajectory and stagewise regularization need not coincide, while the anisotropic example adds a direction-dependent interpretation of the penalties.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link in Section 5.2 and explicit system matrices and numerical parameters for the new anisotropic example. The link is a new access disclosure; its external contents were not inspected. Existing simulation implementation descriptions are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused connections to KL-regularized RL pathologies and path-integral control, including Rudner et al. and Patil et al.; it credits the latter with an existing identity-input special case. Several general optimal-transport/VAE examples disappear. The canonical-divergence and Gaussian-WKL research lineage remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten, including a five-item contribution list. Terminology and density notation are revised throughout, notation moves to the appendix, and future directions receive a separate limitations appendix. Section 5 and the proof appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to two columns, substantially resizing and repositioning figures and equations; Figures 2-4 are regrouped on one page. All eleven figures are retained, with caption, title, and placement edits. V2 also introduces the repeated placeholder running header.

improvement.justification: Corrected formulas, repaired objective normalization, and narrower claims improve accuracy, while the explicit limitations clarify what remains unproved. However, the added empirical support has an internal inconsistency: Appendix C.7 reports the high-noise KL gain [-0.5879, -1.5875], whereas its stated parameters and Riccati equations give approximately [-0.5476, -1.5078]. Geodesic uniqueness remains assumed, and the new proof subsection A.1 is empty. These weaknesses temper the benefits of the expanded theory and clearer exposition.
